title: One DNS record
fullTitle: I Changed One DNS Record and Broke My Website

scenes.sim: SIMULATED DNS MODEL · NO REAL NETWORK
scenes.narration: One edit to the A record for example dot test. Moments later, one client still loads the site and the other cannot connect.
captions: One A-record edit. One client connects, the other cannot.
Same domain, same minute, two different results.

scenes.sim: SIMULATED DNS MODEL · NO REAL NETWORK
scenes.narration: Two steps hide in that failure. Resolution: the client asks its resolver for an address. Connection: it tries to reach that address. Resolution succeeded every time. It returned the wrong destination.
captions: Step one: resolve the name. Step two: connect to the address.
Resolution succeeded. It returned the wrong destination.

scenes.sim: SIMULATED DNS MODEL · NO REAL NETWORK
scenes.narration: Three copies of one answer. The authority now says dot twenty, the wrong address. Resolver A cached dot ten before the edit and trusts it for sixty seconds. Resolver B asked after the edit and cached dot twenty.
captions: Authoritative: .20 (wrong). Resolver A: .10, cached before the edit.
Resolver B asked after the edit and cached .20 for 60 seconds.

scenes.sim: SIMULATED DNS MODEL · NO REAL NETWORK
scenes.narration: At thirty seconds the source is corrected back to dot ten. Client A still connects. Client B still fails. Fixing the record changed nothing for a cache already full.
captions: Client B still fails. The fix changed nothing for a full cache.

scenes.sim: SIMULATED DNS MODEL · NO REAL NETWORK
scenes.narration: Resolver B stored the wrong answer at fifteen with a sixty second TTL, so it expires at seventy five. Lowering the TTL now does not shorten that. Expiry pushes nothing; it only allows the next question.
captions: Cached at t=15 with TTL 60: expires at t=75, whatever you change now.
Expiry permits a new lookup. It pushes nothing.

scenes.sim: SIMULATED DNS MODEL · NO REAL NETWORK
scenes.narration: Advance the clock. At sixty, resolver A's entry has aged out and its next query fetches dot ten. At seventy five, resolver B's bad entry lapses, and because a client asks, it fetches the corrected record.
captions: t=60: resolver A refreshes on its next query.
t=75: resolver B's bad entry lapses; the next query fetches .10.

scenes.sim: SIMULATED DNS MODEL · NO REAL NETWORK
scenes.narration: Ten queries. Zero resolution failures. Four failed connections, all to the wrong address. Resolver A recovered at sixty, resolver B at seventy five. No single propagation time. Real networks add browser caches, system caches and AAAA records this model omits.
captions: Resolver A recovered at t=60, resolver B at t=75. No single propagation time.
Not modelled: browser and OS caches, serve-stale, prefetch, AAAA.

scenes.narration: Fixing the source does not erase every cached answer. And a record TTL says nothing about how long your pages are cached. That is a separate clock.
captions: Fixing the source does not erase every cached answer.
Record TTL is not content-cache lifetime. Separate clocks.
